second_order: calling the room to make the LOST numbers
theme_note: Across several otherwise separate posts, people recruit help to put 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42 on r/place; the calls vary from a bare invitation to a plea after one person has struggled alone.

second_order: placing the numbers together and settling how they look
theme_note: Participants turn a call into a shared build by locating it, joining, reporting pieces complete, choosing dark rather than light green, and proposing further marks; what varies is whether they coordinate live or show another attempt.

second_order: celebrating that they did it and are somewhere on the canvas
theme_note: Completion becomes something to announce, screenshot, take pride in, and treat as belonging to the larger canvas; some celebrate the work itself while others value simply having something visible there.

second_order: keeping the numbers clean and noticeable
theme_note: After finishing, people shift to maintenance: refusing expansion, watching hostile changes, repairing individual digits, recruiting cleaners, and judging visibility; the threats range from random pixels to deliberate multi-account or swastika changes.

second_order: staying peaceful and helping neighbouring art
theme_note: People protect their mark through peace treaties, borders, reciprocal spare turns, warnings and confirmation, and direct help moving nearby art; within this practice they also debate a proposed takeover before choosing not to make enemies.

second_order: working LOST jokes and rituals into the canvas
theme_note: Participants make the work locally recognizable by joking about candidates, the show's ending, the 108-minute interval and 'Execute'; the allusions variously ease maintenance, narrate completion, or imagine repeating the mark.

second_order: redirecting scattered number-making to the existing numbers
theme_note: Separate efforts to make a more prominent set meet replies pointing people back to the already completed numbers and asking them to maintain it instead; the alternative attempts remain visible rather than being treated as the same coordinated build.

Once placement ends, people recount survival, damaged digits, relief, ease of defence, lasting vulnerability and happiness; assessments vary from accepting a griefed six to claiming history and a continuing LOST presence.

second_order: working out whether endless pixels were a glitch
theme_note: A final exchange asks why the wait disappeared and answers that apparent placements probably did not register; this canvas-mechanics check belongs with no other practice in the record.
